etymologies.etymologyHTML: From member +‎ -ship.

definitions.definition: The state of being a member of a group or organization.

quote.citation: 1999, Andrew Pyper, chapter 10, in Lost Girls:
quote.text: But when Krystal McConnell and Ashley Flynn were named deep in the heart of the '80s the thing was cuteness, feminine delicacy raised to an aesthetic paradigm. --- And everyone named according to a particular version of the pedigree fantasy. Ashley : transplanted Southern privilege, a destiny lying in sorority mixers and a marriage of health club memberships, state-of-the-art appliances and night courses in nouvelle cuisine.

quote.citation: 2012, The Etiquette of Freemasonry: A Handbook for the Brethren, →ISBN:
quote.text: Hence there resulted a division of the membership of the brotherhood into two classes, the practical and theoretic, or, as they are more commonly called, the operative and speculative, or “domatic” and “geomatic."

definitions.definition: The body of members of an organization.
(mathematics) The fact of being a member of a set.
(transitive, sociolinguistics) To classify (someone) as belonging to a certain group or community.

quote.citation: 1975 April, Malcolm Coulthard, “Discourse Analysis in English – A Short Review of the Literature”, in Language Teaching, volume 8, number 2, →DOI, page 83:
quote.text: Whatever the topic of the conversation the speaker must ‘membership’ his listener, put him into one of two or more mutually exclusive boxes. Each time a topic changes the listener must be re-membershipped, and during a conversation the same person may be membershipped as a doctor, a rugby player, a liberal, a gardener, a bridge player.
